description:
discover_crl_signer (pkix-revocation/src/signer_discovery.rs:87-113) returns the FIRST cert in bundle order that matches AKI/SKI; falls through to FIRST cert that matches issuer-DN if no AKI present.

Existing tests (aki_ski_picks_correct_rollover_signer, aki_ski_is_order_independent) verify order-independence ONLY for the case where one bundle cert has matching SKI and others share its subject DN. They do NOT exercise:

1. Two bundle certs with byte-identical SKI (improbable but possible — SKI is a hash truncation in some profiles). Discovery returns the first; semantics are first-wins. No test asserts this.
2. AKI absent, issuer-DN fallback, multiple bundle certs sharing the CRL issuer DN. Discovery returns the first. For the §4.5 PKITS case AKI is always present, so this path is untested.

Add tests:
1. Bundle order [A, B] where both A and B have matching SKI bytes. Assert discover returns A.
2. Bundle of [bridge_cert, new_key_cert] where the CRL has no AKI (synthetic — strip the AKI from the CRL before parsing, or use a different CRL fixture). Assert discover returns the first DN-matching cert.

These are not bug reports; they are coverage gaps that allow future refactors to silently change first-wins semantics without test failure.
title: Bundle order sensitivity in discover_crl_signer not exercised by tests
